【Aspect-ratio composition routes】
Aspect-ratio composition routes

Apply exactly one route beneath . The ratio changes framing behavior, not the inherited five layers, 40–60% content-bearing breathing air, measurable scale, railing-free architecture, or figure and costume rules.

16:9 — default cinematic landscape

• Use for balanced establishing shots, architecture plus landscape, and general cinematic scenes.
• Spread the fixed five layers across a balanced cinematic width and favor an off-center ruling subject near a thirds intersection.
• Allow a strong diagonal, one-point corridor, centered axis, or framed vista.
• Keep environment-led scale-marker figures around 1–4% of frame height; use 5–8% only when the full silhouette must read, and never enlarge them merely because the frame is wide.
• Preserve breathing room for sky, cloud volume, reflections, or distant islands.
• For celestial-city oppression, keep the horizon near the lower third, use a distant low or eye-level camera, and let the principal mass dominate the middle and upper frame. A wide canvas does not imply an aerial view.

Prompt cue: 16:9 横向电影画幅，宽阔建立镜头，五层空间与有内容空气清晰.

21:9 — panoramic spectacle

• Use for immense cloud seas, floating-island chains, long bridges, processions, and lateral architecture.
• Spread environment storytelling horizontally while keeping one dominant anchor.
• Use foreground elements at one or both edges to prevent an empty strip-like frame.
• Keep vertical landmarks away from being cropped; reduce their relative height.
• Use layered lateral rhythm rather than filling the center with many objects.
• For palace density and pressure, favor low-viewpoint telephoto compression across the width; do not turn the panorama into a top-down city map.

Prompt cue: 21:9 超宽银幕画幅，横向展开的史诗尺度，边缘框景与远景层叠.

4:3 — classical tableau

• Use for formal architecture, courtyards, pavilions, symmetrical gates, and storybook-like cinematic tableaux.
• Favor centered symmetry, stable triangles, or slightly off-center one-point perspective.
• Allocate more vertical space than 16:9 for roofs, clouds, trees, and reflections.
• Keep the composition stately and dense without crowding the corners.

Prompt cue: 4:3 古典横幅画幅，稳定庄严的空间组织，建筑与天空比例均衡.

3:2 — photographic film still

• Use for naturalistic cinematic stills, diagonal movement, travel moments, and environment-led character scenes.
• Favor asymmetrical thirds, leading lines, believable lens placement, and less formal staging.
• Keep foreground-to-midground transitions natural and avoid excessively perfect symmetry unless requested.

Prompt cue: 3:2 摄影横幅画幅，自然电影剧照构图，非对称三分法与明确引导线.

4:5 — editorial portrait canvas

• Use for tall gates, pavilion facades, waterfalls, ancient trees, fashion-led environment scenes, and poster-like compositions.
• Stack foreground, subject, anchor, and sky vertically.
• Keep important architecture away from side crops; use a narrower path or staircase as the depth axis.
• If people remain scale markers, place them in the lower third and keep the landmark dominant.
• Reserve controlled space above the anchor for cloud, canopy, or light shafts.

Prompt cue: 4:5 竖幅画面，纵向层叠构图，下方人物尺度参照，上方建筑与天光主导.

9:16 — immersive vertical spectacle

• Use for soaring towers, heavenly stairs, cliff waterfalls, giant trees, deep chasms, and mobile-first visuals.
• Build an explicit bottom-to-top reading path. Use vertical repetition and a high or low vanishing point.
• Avoid shrinking a horizontal panorama into the narrow canvas.
• Keep the primary landmark inside the central vertical corridor and use side architecture as framing.
• Limit horizontal island chains and broad group arrangements; prioritize height and ascent.

Prompt cue: 9:16 沉浸式竖屏画幅，自下而上的视觉路径，强烈高度感与纵向空间层叠.

Ratio audit

Before finalizing, verify:

• The prompt names one supported ratio in its first sentence.
• The composition follows that ratio's reading direction.
• The focal anchor is not likely to be cropped.
• Figures remain at the intended scale.
• Negative space is purposeful rather than accidental.
• All five master layers remain readable and 40–60% content-bearing air survives the crop.
• Edges remain railing-free and any people retain the master rear-facing costume grammar.
• Camera height matches the emotional intent; 大全景 and a wide ratio have not been misread as permission for a high-angle view.

Interaction with scale intensity

• Apply ratio first, then scale intensity. Do not change the requested canvas to obtain grandeur.
• Apply camera intent independently from ratio. No supported ratio defaults to bird's-eye or elevated framing.
• For every intensity, retain all five master layers and at least four measurable scale proofs.
• For 史诗级, strengthen the ruling subject and discontinuous comparisons without deleting breathing air.
• For 超宏大, add off-frame or cross-cloud continuation even in 4:5 or 9:16 by stacking the five layers vertically.
• In 21:9, use lateral extreme-distance layers and edge framing; do not scatter many equally large landmarks across the width.
• In 4:5 and 9:16, use lower-third tiny figures, a vertically dominant off-frame structure, and a high or low extreme-distance destination.

Interaction with 仙界大境原典

• Preserve the inherited fixed five layers and 40–60% content-bearing breathing air in every supported ratio; the canon route adds stricter cloud, anchor, motion, and light controls.
• Keep the principal cloud sea below the figure-bearing platform and mainly within the bottom 20–35%, adapting its shape rather than moving it above the architecture.
• Use the ratio only to change reading direction, crop, and placement. Do not change the route's measurable scale, limited far anchors, railing-free architecture, single primary motion, or warm diffuse-light baseline.
• Treat 9:16 as one vertical image by default. Never infer nine images, a sequence, a collage, or a figure-distribution schedule from the ratio.


【Celestial grand-realm canon route】
Celestial grand-realm canon route

Use  first. Apply 仙界大境原典 as a sealed, independent creative route that inherits the shared master scale, five layers, breathing air, architecture, railing, figure, and costume rules, then adds stricter cloud, far-anchor, motion, and warm-light controls. It is not a nine-image series mode and never forces 9:16.

Contents

• Route authority and world promise
• Hard scale system and fixed five-layer space
• Low cloud sea and controlled celestial content
• Optional modules, architecture, immortals, and costume
• Light, color, realism, and ratio adaptation
• Prompt assembly and mandatory audit

Route authority

• Select this route only when the user explicitly says 仙界大境原典, 仙界总则, 仙界原典, or asks to follow the supplied heavenly-realm canon.
• When selected, apply this file after the shared master rules and before all normal scene, visual-style, camera-intent, density, color, and atmosphere defaults. Do not silently blend in 单体仙境, 神域聚居地, 华彩通透仙侠, or 东方苍穹巨构 additions.
• Use the aspect-ratio reference only to adapt reading direction. Use the general composition library only for technical execution that does not conflict with this canon.
• Let explicit user additions extend the route only when they preserve its hard invariants. If an explicit request conflicts, name the conflict instead of quietly replacing the canon.

World promise

Preserve this reading order and mood:

first: immeasurable heavenly architecture -> second: a complete distant celestial realm -> third: a small back-facing immortal -> fourth: a continuing path into unseen heaven

Keep the world 空而不寂，满而不塞，巨而不乱，动而不躁，华丽而克制，通透而安静.

Inherited hard scale system

• Make a principal column diameter equal to roughly five to ten adult heights and its complete height equal to roughly forty to eighty adult heights.
• Make a giant opening, jade screen, portal, or structural aperture equal to roughly twenty to fifty adult heights.
• Let a principal eave span hundreds of body widths and continue beyond the frame.
• Keep human-usable stair risers and bridge surfaces, but let the full stair, bridge, gallery, roofline, or platform cross cloud layers and converge toward an apparently inexhaustible distance.
• Include at least four visible scale proofs in every prompt: an off-frame giant fragment; adult-to-column, portal, screen, or plinth comparison; repeated elements converging into depth; ten to thirty body lengths of open space around the figure; vertically separated palaces; a cloud-sea crossing; near-and-far giant forms; or a distant giant structure shown only in part.

Do not replace these relationships with adjectives such as 宏大 or 史诗 alone.

Inherited fixed five-layer space

Build all five layers even when the ratio changes:

1. A near-camera giant frame: column, eave, screen, pine trunk, cliff, portal edge, or other massive fragment.
2. A broad human-bearing surface: platform, stair, gallery, mirror ground, shallow-water ground, or its open edge.
3. One ruling heavenly megastructure.
4. One to three lighter groups of remote palaces, bridges, platforms, or architectural fragments.
5. A terminal celestial distance: giant moon, low sky light, heavenly river, galaxy, low cloud sea, or boundless clear sky.

• Preserve roughly 40–60% breathing space. Treat it as layered celestial air with value change and distant silhouettes, not blank sky.
• Interleave solid mass and open air. Let sky enter portals, column fields, screens, corridors, and beneath eaves.
• Keep near forms heavier, sharper, darker, and more detailed; make distance lighter, softer, lower-contrast, and more generalized without turning it gray.

Low cloud sea and local mist

• Keep the main cloud sea below the architectural platform level. Its top must remain below the figure's feet and platform edge.
• Let the cloud sea occupy mainly the bottom 20–35% of the image, with rounded, thick, clustered cumulus volume and a stable low horizon.
• Keep people, platforms, plinths, columns, corridors, screens, eaves, and roofs fully above the main cloud layer.
• Keep the upper sky and the air around figures clear and transparent.
• Distinguish local fairy mist from the cloud sea. Allow only thin, translucent, nearly colorless mist beneath foundations, beside waterfalls, or between selected distance layers. Never wrap the whole city in fog.

Controlled celestial content

Give each image exactly:

• one ruling megastructure;
• one far-realm anchor;
• one primary dynamic phenomenon or quiet sign of life;
• one near scale reference;
• one or a few immortals.

Select one or two compatible far relationships, not a catalog: remote giant palace fragments, an extremely long sky bridge, receding halls along the cloud edge, a lit gate silhouette, a transparent waterfall, an arc wall, a heavenly river, one crane before a moon, or separated floating platforms.

Use only one primary motion system: a cloud waterfall, transparent water fall, heavenly river, shallow-water ripple, wind-driven banner or veil, one crane, a high-altitude water channel, or thin cloud flow beneath a platform. Make it slow, broad, gravity-aware, and subordinate to architectural stillness.

Optional world modules

• Giant moon: optional per image. When selected, use a realistic lunar surface, maria, craters, and terminator; occupy about 25–50% of frame width; place it low, off-center, partially cropped, or divided by architecture.
• Ancient welcome pine: optional, never automatic. Use a trunk diameter of roughly one to three adult heights and a crown spanning twenty to forty body widths. Let an off-frame trunk or long branch frame rather than decorate the scene.
• Ground: choose one coherent type: a thin transparent water film with restrained ripples; an immense edgeless mirror platform; shallow-relief white-stone stairs; a polished suspended platform; a curved shallow waterway ending in a fall; or a broad empty jade plane.

Heavenly architecture

• Use Chinese spatial order without reconstructing a specific dynasty.
• Recompose extended eaves, colossal column fields, moon openings, giant stone screens, corridors, heavenly stairs, layered roofs, cloud platforms, and suspended gates into a unique celestial language.
• Keep architecture immense, simple, quiet, and structurally legible: large uninterrupted material planes, few organizing lines, repeated components for distance, and broad plain surfaces for weight.
• Concentrate decoration in one local zone. Use large shallow reliefs derived from cloud flow, water movement, star tracks, moon halos, wind marks, or celestial arcs; keep the remaining surfaces calm.
• Favor heavy pale stone, pearl-gray stone, restrained vermilion or ochre timber at roofs and load-bearing tops, narrow pale-gold ridge lines, and selective mineral religious color near upper structures.
• Use no railing of any kind on ground, bridges, platforms, stairs, or architecture unless the user explicitly overrides this canon.

Immortals and costume

• Default to one fictional adult or a very small group, seen from the full back, 30–60 degree rear angle, side-rear walking view, or over-shoulder rear view.
• Default environment-led figures to 1–4% of frame height. Use 5–8% when the full immortal silhouette must read. Use 12–20% only when the user explicitly asks for an over-shoulder or costume-led frame and preserve scale through off-frame architecture and a distant heavenly realm.
• Use calm autonomous actions: slow walking, distant watching, standing at an open platform edge, ascending stairs, entering a curved gallery, relaxed hands, or lightly gathering one sleeve.
• Keep body and hair stable while all cloth responds to one high-altitude wind direction.
• Follow 衣有骨、纱有气、饰有止、色有主: two resilient wind-catching lengths extend from shoulder, arm, or waist; two to four unequal rear hems lag behind movement; a floor-length robe and one vivid trailing outer cape may supply the controlled color accent.

Light, color, and realism

• Light the realm with broad, soft, transparent high-altitude diffusion. Keep the low sun near the horizon or outside the frame so it supplies only gentle direction, warm yellow-gold temperature, and a very thin rim.
• Let the sky act as a giant soft source across stone, jade, timber, roof tile, water, cloth, pine, moon, and cloud sea. Keep highlights warm and delicate and shadows bright, open, and transparent.
• Maintain an overall warm late-afternoon feeling without applying one uniform orange filter. Preserve material separation in pale stone, pearl gray, vermilion or ochre timber, pale gold, clear sky, and garment accents.
• Use large-format architectural-photography and practical film-set realism: stone weight, warm jade translucency, clear timber and roof construction, real bark, water surface tension, continuous water and cloud flow, cumulus volume, cloth gravity and translucency, realistic lunar detail, and credible human proportion.

Ratio adaptation

• For 16:9 and 21:9, extend eaves, galleries, cloud edges, and far anchors laterally while retaining all five layers.
• For 4:3 and 3:2, balance the ruling structure with a broad platform and a clear terminal distance.
• For 4:5 and 9:16, stack the five layers vertically and use stairs, columns, waterfalls, moon arcs, or high openings to maintain the upward reading path.
• Never infer a series, collage, or multi-image output from 9:16. One request produces one prompt unless the user explicitly asks for several.
• Default to a low or human-height camera. Use a high-angle or aerial view only when explicitly requested; never use it merely to show more architecture.

Prompt assembly and audit

Assemble as:

ratio -> camera height, distance, tilt, focal length -> ruling structure -> four or more scale proofs -> fixed five layers -> 40–60% breathing air -> one far anchor -> low cloud sea -> one primary motion -> architecture and ground without railings -> immortal and costume -> broad warm diffuse light -> physical materials -> invariants and exclusions

Before output, verify every answer is yes:

• Is the route explicitly labeled 仙界大境原典 and kept independent?
• Is the requested ratio preserved without any nine-image assumption?
• Are four or more visible scale proofs present with measurable human comparisons?
• Are all five layers assigned and readable?
• Is 40–60% breathing space filled with layered air rather than blankness?
• Is the main cloud sea below the platform and mainly in the bottom 20–35%?
• Are distant palaces limited, lighter, softer, and non-urban in density?
• Is there exactly one ruling structure, one far anchor, and one primary motion or life sign?
• Are all railings absent?
• Are the figure scale, rear-facing angle, costume, and wind direction explicit?
• Is light broad, warm, soft, and transparent rather than hard, gray, or globally orange?
• Do materials and perspective remain physically credible?

If any answer is no, revise before responding. Do not substitute a generic palace city, dense roof carpet, isolated pavilion, gray fog panorama, hard gold backlight, overdecorated historical palace, or automatic megastructure-pressure composition.


【Cinematic xianxia visual DNA】
Cinematic xianxia visual DNA

Use these principles as a transferable visual language beneath . The master scale, five-layer space, breathing air, architecture, railing, figure, and costume rules are mandatory in every route; this file may not weaken them. Do not treat any single subject or palette as mandatory.

Core identity

1. Monumental space with visible evidence: Let architecture, mountain, water, sky, or cloud dominate. Prove size through discontinuous scale bands, partial off-frame structures, negative space, and restrained human scale.
2. One decisive spatial geometry: Make the eye understand the depth path immediately through a vanishing point, symmetry axis, diagonal, curve, frame, or vertical ascent.
3. Eastern construction logic: Use credible beam, bracket, roof, column, open terrace, bridge, stair, courtyard, or garden relationships. Keep edges railing-free unless explicitly requested. Add ornament after structure is clear.
4. Luminous selective chroma: Keep the image bright and color-separated while localizing the highest chroma. Preserve near-neutral pale materials, cool transparent shadows, and clean highlights instead of gray fog, global orange spill, or crushed black.
5. Motivated cinematic light: Establish a believable source, direction, edge response, and atmospheric effect. Use backlight and flare selectively.
6. Layered air: Build foreground, midground, background, and extreme distance with progressively softer contrast and lighter values, while retaining recognizable silhouettes.
7. Material specificity: Distinguish jade, stone, lacquer, wood, bronze, glass, water, silk, cloud, foliage, and gilding through visible surface behavior.
8. Dreamlike plausibility: The world may float or defy gravity, but its perspective, light, construction, reflection, and scale must remain internally coherent.
9. Viewer-subordinate camera: When grandeur means oppression or divine authority, keep the viewer at human height or below the architecture. Use distance and focal length to include the world; do not fly above it merely to show more.

Variable scene families

• Celestial architecture: sky palace, suspended library, star observatory, ritual terrace, heavenly gate.
• Inhabited celestial realms: cloud-borne capitals, nine-heavens settlements, floating-continent palace cities, connected divine-island civilizations, cloud-cliff metropolises.
• Mountain and water: floating peaks, mirror lake, cliff sanctuary, waterfall ravine, cloud-sea harbor.
• Garden fantasy: peach-blossom island, luminous lotus court, ancient pine platform, wisteria bridge.
• Journey spaces: heavenly stair, long bridge, mountain pass, suspended causeway, aerial ferry.
• Sacred landmarks: moon ring, giant bell, celestial instrument, ancient tree, carved gate, crane statue.

Avoid repetitive identity

Do not define the style by repeatedly combining white jade, vermilion columns, blue sky, circular moon gate, cloud reflection, and three female figures. Retain the spatial grandeur, luminous chroma, cinematic light, material refinement, and aerial depth while changing the concrete modules.

Visual treatment families

• 华彩通透仙侠: emphasize luminous material color, intricate ornament, elegant architecture, clean clouds, and a clearly presented scenic world.
• 东方苍穹巨构: emphasize one spatial event, cropped divine architecture, threshold revelation, discontinuous scale, restrained high-key chroma, solitary figures, and low side/backlight. Read its dedicated reference before applying it.

Do not confuse visual treatment with scene scale. Either treatment can direct one landmark or an inhabited celestial realm.

Scale grammar

• Build every intensity with the master five layers, four or more measurable scale proofs, and 40–60% content-bearing breathing air.
• Build 辽阔 by letting layered air, water, cloud gaps, or open courts dominate while the ruling structure remains measurably divine in scale.
• Build 史诗级 by strengthening discontinuous comparisons between the near giant frame, small adult, ruling structure, subordinate realm, and terminal distance.
• Build 超宏大 by letting one colossal element continue beyond the canvas or cross cloud layers while retaining the same five-layer baseline.
• Use a large foreground tree, cliff, column, gate edge, or eave to reveal rather than hide the distant world.
• Avoid placing all architecture and figures on one apparent plane.
• For an inhabited celestial realm, prove scale through continuous urban extent, multiple connected districts, varied skyline height, measurable human comparisons, and architecture in all five layers. Preserve 40–60% air between, below, behind, and through districts; do not reduce it to one landmark plus empty cloud space or erase breathing space with a roof carpet.
• For 繁华压迫, place dense secondary architecture between tiny figures and the dominant megastructure. Let prosperity come from overlap, repetition, circulation, and inhabited detail while the principal mass rises above or hangs over the city.

Desired color language

Useful wording:

• 高明度、选择性高纯度、饱满但克制
• 色块清楚，冷暖关系明确
• 阴影保持透明的蓝灰、青灰或紫灰
• 亮部通透，材质高光干净
• rich but elegant chroma
• luminous saturated colors
• clean color separation
• no gray veil or muddy grading
• no global orange-gold cast
• near-neutral jade and cloud highlights

Avoid relying on high saturation alone. Pair saturation with an area budget, brightness hierarchy, neutral anchors, shadow color, and material realism. High saturation is an accent strategy unless the user explicitly selects 华丽高饱和.


【Composition, color, and light library】
Composition, color, and light library

Select only what supports the scene after applying . This library may vary geometry, camera, palette, and light but may not reduce the fixed five layers, 40–60% content-bearing air, measurable scale, railing-free architecture, or immortal-costume grammar.

Spatial skeletons

• Strict one-point perspective: Put one off-center or centered vanishing point in a deliberate location. Make longitudinal edges converge there; keep verticals parallel; reduce repeated spacing and scale consistently.
• Centered symmetry: Use for gates, palaces, ritual spaces, mirror lakes, and solemn scenes. Add one small asymmetry such as figures, birds, drifting cloth, or foliage to keep it alive.
• Diagonal depth: Lead from a large foreground element toward a smaller midground anchor. Use bridges, stairs, rooflines, shorelines, or light paths.
• S-curve flow: Use winding paths, rivers, cloud belts, bridges, or processions to reveal space gradually.
• Framed vista: Use doors, columns, branches, eaves, cliffs, or fabric at the edge to reveal a luminous distance.
• Vertical ascent: Use for 4:5 and 9:16. Lead from a small lower subject toward a tall gate, tower, waterfall, tree, or light opening.

For 东方苍穹巨构, select the dominant spatial event from its dedicated reference. Treat framing, occlusion, and an architectural mass together as one geometry rather than adding several competing skeletons.

Lens and camera routes

• Wide environmental reveal (20–28mm equivalent): Use a large near frame, deep leading line, and distant landmark to exaggerate separation. Keep verticals controlled and prohibit fisheye distortion.
• Balanced cinematic still (35–50mm equivalent): Use for believable architecture, natural figure scale, and less stylized perspective. Strengthen grandeur through scale bands and off-frame continuation rather than lens distortion.
• Telephoto scale compression (70–100mm equivalent): Use a distant viewpoint to make an immense palace, gate, mountain, or moon dominate the horizon behind a small foreground figure. Separate planes through atmosphere and value, not wide-angle convergence.
• Low camera height: Use for stairs, gates, columns, and towers when upward dominance matters.
• Elevated reveal: Use only when the user explicitly prioritizes bird's-eye geography, city planning, district distribution, or island relationships over embodied pressure. Do not infer it from a cloud sea or city alone.

Do not combine extreme wide-angle distortion with strong telephoto compression in one frame.

Camera priority for prosperity and oppression

When the user wants both a thriving celestial capital and megastructure pressure, choose in this order unless explicit camera instructions override it:

1. Distant low viewpoint + 70–100mm compression: default for dense rooflines, layered districts, and a colossal palace or gate looming behind them. Keep the viewer at terrace, bridge, or human eye height.
2. Distant low viewpoint + 24–35mm rectilinear wide angle: use for approaches, bridges, stairs, gates, column fields, and undersides. Keep enough camera-to-subject distance to avoid meaningless foreground distortion.
3. Human-height threshold + 35–50mm: use for doorways, terraces, cliffs, eaves, interiors, and framed revelations.
4. Elevated overview: use only for an explicit 城市总览 intent.

Do not confuse camera distance with camera height. A far camera can stay below the principal roofline and look slightly upward.

For 繁华压迫, keep the horizon near the lower third, adult figures around 1–3%, a human-bearing threshold in the lower frame, dense subordinate districts across the middle, and an off-frame ruling mass above or behind them. Preserve 40–60% content-bearing air by interleaving sky, portal openings, cloud gaps, void beneath platforms, streets, courts, and atmospheric separation through the city; never trade the master breathing space for a solid roof carpet.

Scale construction

辽阔

• Use all five master layers, four measurable scale proofs, a readable path into distance, and generous content-bearing sky, water, cloud, valley, or courtyard space.
• Figures may be absent or remain secondary.

史诗级 — default

• Use all five master layers and strengthen discontinuity between the near giant frame, known-size adult or threshold, ruling subject, subordinate realm, and terminal distance.
• Include at least four visible proofs, including one direct comparison such as adult-versus-gate, bridge-versus-palace, tree-versus-city, or waterfall-versus-island.
• Keep environment-led scale markers around 1–4% of frame height; use 5–8% only when the full silhouette must read.

超宏大 — macro-scale gate

Require all of the following unless the user explicitly overrides one:

1. All five master layers: near giant frame, human-bearing surface, ruling giant subject, subordinate realm, and terminal celestial distance.
2. Adult scale markers around 1–4% of frame height unless the user explicitly requests stronger narrative presence.
3. One colossal structure that continues beyond at least one frame edge or is partially occluded by a nearer frame.
4. Roughly 40–60% content-bearing breathing air distributed through sky, cloud sea, void, water, open courts, portals, or distance.
5. A visible extreme-distance layer rather than empty fog.
6. Four or more measurable scale proofs and clear value, contrast, or chroma steps between planes; do not place all subjects on one apparent plane.

Treat these as visual evidence, not words to paste mechanically. If the composition cannot satisfy the gate, label it 史诗级 instead of claiming 超宏大.

Focal hierarchy

Use three levels:

1. Dominant: spatial carrier or landmark.
2. Supporting: figures, secondary architecture, foliage, waterfall, or reflected form.
3. Texture: carvings, clouds, birds, petals, small lights, or distant roofs.

Do not assign equal contrast, scale, and detail to all three.

For 神域聚居地, treat the principal palace district or divine axis as the dominant level, supporting districts as the second level, and repeated roofs, bridges, stairs, courtyards, cloud traffic, and small wonders as texture. Preserve density while controlling competition.

Palette recipes

• Clear celestial: azure + jade white + vermilion + warm gold + dark wood.
• Rain-washed garden: emerald + peacock blue + coral + ivory + wet charcoal.
• Bright nocturne: cobalt + violet + restrained magenta + amber gold + moon white; keep blacks open and colored.
• Sunlit mountain: turquoise + pine green + cinnabar + apricot sky + pale stone.
• Sacred dawn: pale cyan + cloud white + saffron gold + mineral red + cool blue-gray shadow.

Aim for two dominant families, one high-chroma accent, and one neutral or dark stabilizer. Avoid using every palette color at equal strength.

Saturation strategies

Use these as starting area budgets, then adapt to the subject:

• 自然鲜明: 70–80% low-to-medium chroma base, 15–25% moderate chroma, up to 5% high-chroma accents.
• 选择性高饱和 — default: 65–75% low-to-medium chroma sky/cloud/jade/stone, 15–25% moderate chroma structure and foliage, 5–10% high-chroma vermilion, coral, garment, flower, or gilded edge accents.
• 华丽高饱和: Allow 15–25% high-chroma areas, but limit equally intense hue families and retain at least one large neutral or dark stabilizer.

Preserve material color separation:

• Keep white jade, cloud highlights, pale stone, and moon white close to neutral.
• Let warm sunlight affect exposed edges and planes; do not wash all materials with the same orange or gold.
• Keep cool shadow colors distinct from warm highlights.
• Reduce distant chroma and contrast progressively without turning distance gray.
• Keep gilding narrow and bright rather than spreading gold across roofs, clouds, skin, and ground.

Lighting recipes

• Low-angle golden backlight: Warm directional light, bright material edges, cool interior shadows, one restrained starburst.
• Rain-cleared daylight: Crisp skylight, wet reflections, saturated foliage, soft sun break, minimal haze.
• Cloud-gap illumination: One shaft highlights the anchor while surrounding space remains luminous, not black.
• Moon and lantern split: Cool blue-violet ambient light plus localized amber light; preserve open shadow detail.
• High-altitude morning: Clean blue skylight, warm grazing highlights, volumetric cloud edges, transparent air.

Material cues

• Jade: subtle internal scattering, mineral veins, polished edges, not uniform plastic.
• Lacquer wood: deep colored body, controlled specular highlights, fine grain at worn edges.
• Gilding: thin accents and raised-edge catches, never coating every surface.
• Bronze: dark patina, warmer worn ridges, crisp relief shadow.
• Glass or glaze: colored transmission, sharp edge highlights, believable thickness.
• Wet stone: darkened base value, broken reflections, localized sheen.
• Silk: directional folds, wind response, soft highlight rolloff.

Failure corrections

• Dull image: increase high-key exposure, color separation, colored shadow detail, and one clear accent; reduce gray mist.
• Cheap neon look: reduce equal-intensity accents, restore ivory/stone/dark stabilizers, and localize the brightest chroma.
• Over-saturated or over-warm image: reduce the area of high-chroma red/gold, restore near-neutral jade and clouds, remove the global orange LUT, and confine warm spill to motivated lit planes.
• Large objects but weak grandeur: add discontinuous scale bands, reduce scale-marker figures, introduce an extreme-distance layer, let one structure continue beyond the frame, and choose either a wide reveal or telephoto compression route.
• Weak perspective: simplify geometry, name one vanishing point, specify repeated scale reduction, and remove competing axes.
• Clutter in 单体仙境: retain one anchor, reduce decorative object types, and separate dominant/supporting/texture levels.
• Clutter in 神域聚居地: retain one ruling district and connected city topology; simplify repeated module types and contrast hierarchy without deleting subordinate districts or urban continuity.
• Plastic architecture: add surface variation, carving depth, edge wear, translucency, patina, grain, and nonuniform reflection.
• Flat distance: create contrast and value steps across foreground, midground, background, and extreme distance.
• Excessive flare: keep one optically motivated flare at a backlit edge and remove decorative flares elsewhere.
• Generic megastructure: crop or occlude the main mass, restore an Eastern human-scale threshold, add a discontinuous scale comparison, reduce equal ornament across giant surfaces, and replace uniform gray grading with high-key warm/cool separation.
• Aerial-map feeling: lower the camera to human or terrace height, restore visible vertical faces and undersides, compress dense palace layers with 70–100mm from a distant viewpoint, lower the horizon, enlarge and crop the principal mass, and keep only an explicit overview request in an elevated view.


【Eastern sky megastructure style】
Eastern sky megastructure style

Use 东方苍穹巨构 as a visual treatment, not a scene category. Apply  first, then add cropping, threshold revelation, and discontinuous scale without weakening the inherited five layers, 40–60% content-bearing air, monumental Eastern language, railing-free edges, or immortal costume. Apply it to either 单体仙境 or 神域聚居地.

Master inheritance

• Map the fixed five layers to: near giant frame or threshold; human-bearing surface with tiny rear-facing immortals; cropped ruling megastructure event; lighter subordinate realm; terminal sky, moon, cloud sea, higher heaven, or extreme-distance settlement.
• Include four or more measurable scale proofs. Cropping alone does not prove size; add adult-to-column, opening, bridge, platform, wall, tree, cliff, or distant-realm comparisons.
• Preserve 40–60% content-bearing air inside and around the event through portals, open courts, void beneath foundations, cloud gaps, water, sky, and distance. Do not confuse a solid gray field with breathing space.
• Keep all thresholds, platforms, bridges, stairs, galleries, and architectural edges railing-free unless explicitly requested.
• When people are present, keep them around 1–4%, rear-facing or rear-oblique, in calm action, with structured immortal clothing and one wind direction.

Core treatment

• Build one dominant spatial event, not one fully visible landmark. Examples: a city beneath an overhanging heavenly gate, a bridge entering an unreachable palace, a waterfall splitting a cloud metropolis, or a divine realm revealed through a circular threshold.
• Show the megastructure as a fragment, underside, wall, gate opening, immense platform, cropped roof mass, vertical foundation, or distant architectural horizon. Continue it beyond at least one frame edge.
• Use deliberate obstruction and threshold viewing. Let eaves, portals, cliff faces, pines, columns, open dark platforms, or cloud gaps reveal the world.
• Make scale discontinuous across the inherited five layers: near giant frame -> human-bearing threshold and tiny adult -> ruling colossal event -> subordinate realm -> terminal distance.
• Preserve internal physical credibility while allowing impossible suspension, inverted weight, cloud-borne foundations, sky waterfalls, and architecture that replaces the horizon.

Composition library

Choose one dominant event geometry; vary it across derivatives.

• Sky-pressure overhang: a cropped gate, palace underside, or enormous platform occupies the upper frame while a city or cloud sea lies below.
• Threshold revelation: a shaded doorway, open terrace, cliff edge, or column field opens onto a much brighter unreachable realm.
• Aperture within the frame: a moon ring, gate opening, arch, paired eaves, or pine-and-cliff gap encloses the distant subject.
• Bridge into the unknowable: a narrow bridge or cloud stair begins near tiny figures and disappears into cloud, light, or the base of a colossal palace.
• Vertical rupture: a waterfall, light shaft, hanging foundation, or sky river cuts through city, cloud, and void.
• Undercroft city reveal: an enormous upper structure floats over a carpet of subordinate roofs and courts.
• Architectural section: use a close or medium view of a giant wall, carved slab, foundation, column field, or partially visible roof system to imply a larger whole.

Do not reuse the moon ring or centered bridge automatically. Select the geometry from the scene promise.

Scale and framing gate

For epic or ultra-macro output, require:

1. One main structure cropped, occluded, or continued outside the frame.
2. Adult scale markers commonly around 1–3% of frame height; use 5–8% only when an explicitly requested full silhouette must read, and preserve rear angle and costume grammar.
3. All five inherited layers and at least four measurable scale proofs, including one direct impossible comparison.
4. A railing-free foreground threshold or human-bearing surface that reveals rather than blocks the principal event.
5. A subordinate realm and readable terminal distance instead of empty fog.
6. Roughly 40–60% content-bearing cloud, void, sky, water, opening, court, or distance that exposes suspension and height without shrinking the architecture into an isolated object.

The megastructure may occupy roughly one-third to two-thirds of the frame, but do not use a fixed percentage when a stronger crop or reveal better serves the event.

Camera

• Default to a viewer-subordinate position: distant low camera or human-height camera, level to slightly upward. Do not default to bird's-eye, aerial, high-angle, or top-down framing.
• Prefer 70–100mm from a distant low viewpoint when the image must combine dense palace-city prosperity with a colossal structure looming behind or above it. Let rooflines, terraces, clouds, and the main mass compress into a heavy layered wall of civilization.
• Use 24–32mm rectilinear lenses for bridge approaches, low viewpoints, column fields, gates, and underside reveals. Keep the camera far enough away to preserve a readable hierarchy.
• Use 35–50mm for portals, terraces, interiors, and believable architectural fragments at human height.
• Default to deep focus with controlled verticals. Use atmosphere, overlap, and contrast steps rather than bokeh to separate planes.
• Keep the camera distant enough that wide-angle perspective reveals the spatial hierarchy instead of turning the nearest surface into meaningless distortion.
• Use an elevated overview only when the user explicitly asks to understand the city's geographic layout. Never choose it merely because the scene contains clouds, islands, or many buildings.

For a 繁华压迫 frame, keep the horizon near the lower third, put tiny figures and the viewing threshold along the lower edge, compress dense secondary districts across the middle, and let the cropped principal megastructure dominate the middle and upper frame. The viewer should feel beneath or in front of the structure, never above it.

High-key restrained color

Create luminosity through value and temperature before increasing saturation:

• Keep about 65–80% of the frame in pale stone, cloud white, muted jade, blue-gray sky, cool water, or other low-to-medium chroma luminous bases.
• Use about 15–25% moderate color in slate blue, mineral green, dark timber, subdued vermilion, or weathered bronze.
• Reserve the strongest warm chroma for about 3–8% of sunlit roof edges, lacquer accents, garments, banners, or metal catches unless the user explicitly asks for more.
• Keep the scene high in brightness with clean color separation. Low chroma must never become muddy gray, beige haze, or dead grading.
• Preserve explicit high-saturation requests by expanding material color selectively while retaining a large neutral sky, cloud, stone, water, or shadow stabilizer.

Light and atmosphere

• Favor a low sun from the side or rear, commonly near dawn or late afternoon, with warm ivory, pale apricot, or restrained gold highlights.
• Use cool high-altitude skylight as the ambient fill; keep shadows open in cyan-gray, slate blue, blue-green, or violet-gray.
• Let thin localized mist scatter light around thresholds, waterfalls, foundations, and cloud edges. Never apply a uniform fog veil.
• Use soft highlight rolloff and visible material edge response. Avoid blown-out white clouds and black architectural undersides.
• Omit lens flare by default; allow one faint optically motivated flare only when it strengthens the threshold event.

Material direction

Favor monumental pale stone, weathered jade, carved cliff-like foundations, matte mineral surfaces, restrained lacquer timber, dark bronze, narrow gilded edges, water, and dense volumetric cloud. Reduce ornamental variety on the largest masses; place fine Chinese detail on thresholds, rooflines, doors, column bases, and human-scale surfaces so the structure reads as architecture rather than abstract concrete.

Prompt order

Assemble as:

ratio and camera -> inherited measurable scale proofs -> fixed five layers and 40–60% content-bearing air -> scene route -> dominant spatial event -> crop or occlusion -> railing-free human threshold -> monumental Eastern construction and localized detail -> rear-facing immortals and costume grammar -> high-key restrained palette -> low side/backlight -> localized atmospheric scattering -> deep-focus cinematic material rendering -> global and route invariants

Audit

Revise if any answer is no:

• Is the focal idea a spatial event rather than a catalog of objects?
• Are all five inherited layers readable with 40–60% content-bearing air?
• Are four or more measurable scale proofs present beyond cropping alone?
• Does at least one structure feel larger than the frame?
• Do threshold, occlusion, and scale markers reveal the world intentionally?
• Are figures small enough to function as evidence rather than protagonists?
• When figures are present, are rear angle, calm action, structured immortal clothing, and one wind direction explicit?
• Is the image luminous without relying on high saturation everywhere?
• Are warm highlights localized and cool shadows transparent?
• Does mist sculpt depth without hiding the architecture?
• Is the result recognizably Eastern without looking like a historical reconstruction, European castle, modern megacity, or sci-fi concrete monolith?
• Does the camera remain subordinate to the megastructure, and was any high-angle overview explicitly requested?
• Are all edges railing-free unless the user explicitly requested railings?

Avoid a fully visible palace centered in empty clouds, default bird's-eye or aerial city views, dense red-and-gold theme-park color, excessive filigree on every giant surface, identical stamped roofs, muddy blue-gray grading, opaque fog, crushed black foregrounds, fisheye distortion, multiple equal wonders, or a tiny picturesque pavilion that lacks megastructure evidence.


【Inhabited celestial realm route】
Inhabited celestial realm route

Use this route to design a place where immortals plausibly live at mythic scale. Apply  first; city density and topology may expand but never replace its scale, five layers, breathing air, architecture, railing, figure, or costume rules. The result is not a historical reconstruction and not a lone palace floating above clouds.

Route promise

Prioritize in this order:

1. Mythic invention: make the world impossible in reality through floating continents, kilometer-scale cloud cities, vertical heavens, suspended transit, celestial waterfalls, divine trees, star rivers, or other coherent wonders.
2. Eastern recognition: express the civilization through flying eaves, bracket sets, layered roofs, open terraces, courtyards, gates, towers, galleries, stairs, lacquered timber, mineral pigments, bronze, jade, and restrained gilding.
3. Cinematic credibility: keep one perspective system, motivated light, physical materials, volumetric clouds, scale comparisons, and readable spatial continuity.

Do not let historical building practice cap the scale or geometry. Use it as vocabulary and ordering logic only.

Master inheritance

• Map the fixed five layers to: near giant threshold; broad inhabited circulation surface; one ruling district or divine axis; connected subordinate districts; extreme-distance settlement, higher heaven, or terminal sky.
• Preserve 40–60% content-bearing air between, below, behind, and through districts. Use courtyards, streets, portals, cloud gaps, open water, void beneath platforms, and atmospheric separation; do not replace breathing air with a continuous roof carpet.
• Include at least four measurable scale proofs. Use adult-to-column, gate, platform, bridge, tree, cliff, or city-axis comparisons in addition to density and repetition.
• Keep all platforms, bridges, stairs, galleries, terraces, streets, and cloud harbors railing-free unless the user explicitly requests a railing.
• When inhabitants are visible, default them to 1–4% rear-facing or rear-oblique adults with calm actions, structured immortal clothing, and one coherent wind direction. City activity may multiply tiny figures but may not turn them into front-facing portraits or generic silhouettes.
• Keep the largest city structures immense, calm, and structurally legible. Concentrate fine ornament at human-readable thresholds instead of coating every giant surface.

Ensemble hierarchy

Replace the single-landmark rule with one ruling hierarchy:

• Establish one principal palace district, divine axis, city crown, sacred mountain core, or elevated imperial precinct as the dominant mass.
• Add two to four subordinate districts with lower scale or contrast.
• Use many minor roofs, towers, courtyards, open terraces, bridges, stairs, waterfalls, and cloud harbors as urban texture.
• Connect districts visibly. A settlement must show circulation or infrastructure rather than unrelated monuments scattered in fog.
• Vary roof height, platform elevation, spacing, overlap, and orientation. Avoid identical stamped buildings.

High density is desirable; equal visual dominance is not. Reduce clutter through hierarchy, repetition, and connected spatial logic instead of deleting the city.

World topologies

Choose one topology that fits the request; do not default repeatedly to the same composition.

• Axial ascension: gates, courts, terraces, and palace districts rise toward a high celestial crown.
• Terraced floating continent: a vast airborne landmass carries cascading city levels, cliff palaces, waterfalls, and lower cloud docks.
• Suspended island network: several inhabited islands connect through long bridges, flying galleries, cloud ferries, and ceremonial causeways.
• Nine-heavens stack: multiple inhabited strata float above one another, each smaller, brighter, or more sacred toward the summit.
• Divine-axis ring city: districts encircle a colossal tree, pillar, mountain, star instrument, sun wheel, or waterfall shaft without turning it into a Western sci-fi megastructure.
• Cloud-cliff metropolis: palaces cling to immense vertical cliffs and continue above, below, and beyond the frame.
• Horizon palace belt: a laterally continuous skyline of courts and towers stretches across a cloud ocean, suitable for 16:9 or 21:9 spectacle.

Ensemble macro gate

For an epic or ultra-macro inhabited realm, require visible evidence:

1. Show the fixed five layers: near giant threshold, human-bearing circulation surface with tiny inhabitants, ruling district, connected subordinate districts, and an extreme-distance settlement or higher heaven.
2. Keep environment-led adults around 1–4% of frame height; use 5–8% only when a full silhouette must read.
3. Let architecture continue beyond a side, top, lower cloud layer, or horizon so the settlement feels larger than the frame.
4. Usually spread the built world across most of the usable width and maintain architecture in near, middle, and far planes. Do not isolate one palace inside an empty cloud field.
5. Use one principal mass, two to four supporting masses, and numerous small architectural repetitions.
6. Include connective evidence such as corridors, bridges, stairs, terraces, cloud roads, ferry platforms, or aqueduct-like waterfalls.
7. Place clouds between, below, and behind districts. Use gaps and illuminated edges so clouds reveal scale rather than erase buildings.
8. Preserve roughly 40–60% content-bearing air. Distribute it through open courts, streets, portal air, water, cloud gaps, void beneath platforms, and separation between vertical districts rather than reserving one empty sky block.

If the frame only shows one palace, one gate, or one platform, route it back to 单体仙境 even when the prompt says 天宫.

Camera and clarity

• For 繁华压迫, favor a distant low or human-height camera with 70–100mm compression so dense palace layers accumulate behind tiny figures and beneath the ruling megastructure.
• Use a distant low 24–35mm rectilinear lens for approaches, bridges, stairs, gates, and underside reveals; use 35–50mm at human height for threshold views and believable architectural proportions.
• For low-angle grandeur, keep the camera low but far enough away to reveal the whole city hierarchy; control vertical convergence and prohibit fisheye distortion.
• Default to deep focus and large depth of field. Keep the near threshold, human-bearing surface, principal district, subordinate districts, and terminal distance readable.
• Use elevated reveals only when the user explicitly selects 城市总览 or asks for bird's-eye geography, district relationships, or island distribution. Do not infer elevation from 大全景, 云海, 浮岛, or 仙城.
• Use atmosphere through smaller scale, cooler distance, and stepped contrast. Do not create depth by applying a uniform gray fog layer.
• Keep foreground viewing platforms subordinate, commonly around 8–15% of frame area, detached from the edges when requested, and never blocking the principal city mass.

Prosperity under pressure

Express prosperity without an aerial map:

• Place tiny rear-facing immortals and a human-bearing threshold in the lower frame; give principal scale markers structured robes and one coherent wind direction.
• Fill the middle distance with overlapping roofs, courts, bridges, galleries, cloud traffic, waterfalls, terraces, lights, and processional movement.
• Place one ruling palace, gate, platform, wall, or divine axis behind or above those districts; crop it with the top or side edge so it remains immeasurable.
• Keep visible vertical faces, foundations, columns, and undersides. Roof coverage alone proves density but not pressure.
• Keep the horizon low and let the city continue beyond both the frame and the cloud layers.

Fantasy density without generic fantasy

Add two to four mutually coherent impossible systems, not a random catalog:

• palaces embedded in floating mountain continents;
• waterfalls falling through several cloud strata;
• cloud stairs and suspended galleries connecting districts;
• a higher heaven or distant divine capital visible beyond the main city;
• enormous celestial trees, bells, star instruments, sun wheels, or jade pillars integrated into the urban plan;
• cloud harbors, crane routes, flying boats, light bridges, or ritual processions that imply habitation;
• inverted peaks, hanging gardens, airborne rivers, or luminous cloud channels governed by the same world logic.

Avoid European castles with Chinese roofs, modern skyscraper grids, sci-fi neon skylines, game-map clutter, or a historical palace merely pasted onto clouds.

Palace-color realism

Use a 华彩但不过曝 material route when the user wants vivid color:

• Allow vermilion lacquer, mineral green and blue painting, gilded or bronze roof details, white jade, dark wood, colored glaze, and bright sky to remain visibly saturated.
• Separate saturation by material instead of reducing all architecture to accent color.
• Keep clouds, pale stone, and white jade near-neutral; use them as luminous stabilizers.
• Confine warm gold to sunlit edges, roof ridges, metal, and selected lit planes. Do not apply a global orange-gold wash.
• Keep shadows transparent cyan, blue-gray, blue-green, or violet-gray according to the lighting premise.
• Preserve high visibility, clean color separation, and readable distant silhouettes; prohibit muddy gray grading.

Prompt assembly

Order a 神域聚居地 prompt as:

ratio -> camera height, distance, tilt, and focal length -> inherited measurable scale proofs -> fixed five layers and 40–60% content-bearing air -> impossible inhabited-world premise -> chosen topology -> ruling and subordinate districts -> railing-free connective infrastructure -> monumental Eastern construction and localized ornament -> tiny rear-facing immortals and costume grammar -> vivid material palette -> one motivated light source -> discrete volumetric clouds and high-visibility atmosphere -> deep-focus cinematic rendering -> global and route invariants

Group architecture by district and depth rather than stacking a long unstructured list of nouns.

Route audit

Reject or revise the prompt if any answer is no:

• Does the scene depict a lived-in world rather than one decorative landmark?
• Are all five inherited layers readable with 40–60% content-bearing air?
• Are four or more measurable scale proofs present beyond density alone?
• Do buildings remain present across near, middle, far, and extreme-distance planes?
• Is one principal hierarchy clearly dominant without deleting subordinate districts?
• Are districts visibly connected?
• Does scale come from mass, quantity, height, continuity, and tiny inhabitants together?
• Do clouds reveal the city instead of hiding it?
• Are material colors vivid but separated from the lighting grade?
• Would the city still feel immense if the figures were removed?
• Does the result remain recognizably Eastern without becoming a historical reconstruction?
• Are all edges railing-free unless the user explicitly requested railings?
• When people are present, are rear angle, scale, calm action, immortal costume, and one wind direction explicit?
• If the goal is prosperity and pressure, is the viewer below or at human height rather than above the city?
• Was any elevated overview explicitly requested rather than inferred from the desire to show scale?

Preserve user parameters and avoid copying unnecessary elements.

Eastern sky megastructure input pattern

画幅比例：16:9
场景路由：神域聚居地
视觉风格路由：东方苍穹巨构

主导空间事件：一座延伸出画面的巨型天门悬压在下层密集宫城上方，人物、连续屋脊、次级宫阙与天门形成尺度断裂
